canonical_topic: Heating Degree Days (HDD) and Cooling Degree Days (CDD)
definition: HDD and CDD are daily measures of how far the average temperature deviates from a reference baseline, used as the underlying index for most weather derivatives.
core_idea: HDDs accumulate on cold days when heating is needed (temperature below baseline), and CDDs accumulate on hot days when cooling is needed (temperature above baseline); the daily values are summed over a contract period and compared to a strike to determine payoff.
key_points: HDD and CDD contracts are the most common form of weather derivative
Common baseline temperatures are 65°F in the United States and 18°C in Europe
Example: an 85°F average daily temperature against a 65°F baseline contributes 20 CDD
Daily HDD/CDD values are accumulated over the contract period and compared against a strike to compute the payoff
relationships: HDD/CDD accumulated over a period is compared to a contract Strike to compute the payoff of an HDD/CDD weather derivative
trading_implications: Payoff sensitivity depends on the chosen baseline and reference weather station, both of which are specified in the contract

variables.Average Temperature: observed daily average temperature at the reference station
